title: Sidecar recovery reports success after copy or hash repair fails
observed_behavior: Repair-PendingSidecarArtifacts catches and logs every Copy-SrtAtomic failure or recovered-file SHA-256 mismatch, then returns only the unchanged manifest. Its caller snapshots sidecarCandidates before repair and defines wasRecovered as either a parked_recovered state or sidecarCandidates.Count greater than zero. Therefore a trusted missing sidecar whose original exists is reported in recovered_count, row status recovered, and the recovery result event even when the copy failed or the copied file was deleted after a hash mismatch.
expected_invariant: Pending-publish recovery counters, row status, reason text, and durable result events must report recovery only after every claimed artifact satisfies its verified postcondition; a failed repair must remain failed or review-blocked with actionable evidence.
root_cause: The sidecar repair helper erases per-artifact outcomes by swallowing exceptions and returning only the manifest, while the summary layer treats pre-repair candidate existence as proof of post-repair success instead of checking the local sidecar or consuming a structured repair result.
failure_scenario: A transient copy error, permission problem, disk-full condition, or hash mismatch occurs while recovering a missing parked subtitle sidecar from original_local_file. The local sidecar remains absent, but preflight recovery reports one recovered item with an empty reason and emits a recovered event. The later drain validator remains fail-closed on the missing sidecar, so media is preserved, but the recovery evidence misdirects the operator, obscures the actual repair failure, and can repeat indefinitely without a truthful failed_count.
evidence: pending_repair.ps1 lines 33-49 catches Copy-SrtAtomic and SHA-256 verification failures and only writes a warning.
pending_repair.ps1 line 51 returns the manifest without any success/failure or per-sidecar outcome.
pending_repair.ps1 lines 324-331 captures candidates solely from the pre-repair missing-local/original-exists condition.

pending_repair.ps1 lines 371-384 calls the lossy helper and then marks recovery from sidecarCandidates.Count rather than a verified postcondition, incrementing recovered_count and leaving reason blank.
A structured search across every current finding fragment found no existing record for this candidate-based false recovery accounting.
Focused tests assert successful recovered_count behavior and stale-drain cleanup but do not inject Copy-SrtAtomic failure or recovered-sidecar hash mismatch in this branch.
affected_flows: pending-publish recovery summaries and operator diagnostics
subtitle sidecar recovery and repeated repair attempts
existing_safeguards: Manifest and sidecar trust checks run before recovery.
Copy-SrtAtomic is used and the recovered local sidecar is SHA-256 checked.
A hash mismatch removes the bad recovered file.
The later drain path independently validates required sidecars and remains fail-closed.
safeguard_gap: Those controls protect publication bytes but do not preserve truthful recovery state: the exception is swallowed and neither the summary nor the event distinguishes a verified repair from an attempted one.
tests_present: ops/pipeline/tests/Unit/Invoke-PendingPublishTransactionFaultInjectionChecks.ps1 covers successful sidecar-placement crash reconciliation and other stale-drain failures.
tests_missing: Copy-SrtAtomic returns Ok=false for a trusted sidecar candidate and recovery reports failed/review rather than recovered.
Recovered local sidecar hash mismatch reports failure, retains actionable reason evidence, and does not increment recovered_count.
Mixed multi-sidecar outcomes produce truthful per-artifact and aggregate counts/events.
recommended_remediation: Return a structured result from Repair-PendingSidecarArtifacts with attempted, recovered, failed, and reason evidence per sidecar. Derive wasRecovered and aggregate counters from verified results or an explicit post-repair existence/hash check, and emit failed or review status with the captured reason whenever any selected repair fails. Add focused fault-injection tests for copy failure, hash mismatch, and mixed batches.
remediation_risk: medium: this changes recovery result/event semantics and callers must preserve current fail-closed drain behavior, trust checks, retry evidence, and compatibility for successful recovery
validation_rung: Focused PowerShell pending-publish safety and transaction fault-injection tests with disposable synthetic media/sidecar bytes; representative real-media validation is not required unless artifact-copy or drain policy is also changed.
prior_audit_relationship: Distinct from current W04 destination-lock and sidecar-manifest append findings and from W15 manifest trust findings; structured current-ledger search found no matching root cause or failure scenario.

title: Disabling one movie filter category re-enables global deletion for every other category
observed_behavior: The verified metadata-tail path is selected only when every filter option is true. Setting any one category false switches the whole cleaner to legacy global substitutions for all categories that remain enabled, so metadata-like words in the actual title are deleted and a valid title can become empty.
expected_invariant: A disabled filter category must affect only that category, while enabled metadata categories remain constrained to verified release-tail evidence and preserve title-region words.
root_cause: The branch at line 629 treats all-enabled configuration as a proxy for the safe tail-aware algorithm. Per-category configurability is implemented in a separate global-regex fallback instead of parameterizing the verified-tail detector.
failure_scenario: An operator disables audio-channel filtering to preserve an unusual tag. The WebView/backend preview now changes The.Web.2013.mkv from The Web (2013) to The (2013); disabling languages/subs filtering changes Atmos.Fear to Fear, The.Remux to The, and AVC.2024 to an empty result. A confirmed rename can therefore discard real title identity merely because an unrelated category was disabled.
evidence: movie.py lines 629-641 use _movie_title_before_verified_tail only when all(filter_options.values()) is true.
movie.py lines 642-670 globally apply regex/token removal for every still-enabled category after any option is false.
Bundled-Python current-byte reproductions returned The (2013), Fear (2024), The (2024), and an empty string for the cited cases.
CHANGELOG MP-CHANGE-2026-0712-018 states that global movie token deletion was replaced with title preservation plus verified metadata-tail cleaning.

Current tests preserve metadata-like title words only under all-default options; disabled-category tests use a generic Movie title and do not combine an unrelated disabled option with title-like metadata tokens.
Structured current-finding searches found no matching configuration-triggered fallback defect.
affected_flows: destination naming and later library matching
existing_safeguards: Rename apply requires strict backend confirmation and a current preview fingerprint.
The default all-enabled configuration uses the safer verified-tail path.
An empty computed title blocks or degrades preview rather than silently inventing a title.
safeguard_gap: The preview faithfully exposes the corrupted name but does not explain that an unrelated option caused title deletion; confirmation cannot restore title identity an operator reasonably expects the documented cleaner to preserve.
tests_present: tests/python/desktop/test_service_rename_movie.py covers title-like metadata terms under defaults and separately covers disabled filter categories.
tests_missing: Each single disabled category combined with title words matching every other category.
Parity assertion that per-category options never change the title region before a verified metadata tail.
Regression that disabling one category cannot turn AVC.2024 or another nonempty title into an empty name.
recommended_remediation: Use the verified-tail algorithm for every option combination and make its evidence/category selection honor enabled flags independently. Remove the global fallback, then add a matrix that disables each category while exercising title words matching all remaining category patterns.
remediation_risk: medium: movie naming is a high-risk mutation surface and cleaner changes can alter many previews; retain strict preview fingerprints and compare a broad bad-case corpus before apply
validation_rung: Focused movie cleaner, rename planner/preview/apply, cleaning-policy fingerprint, and Python/PowerShell naming-parity tests using synthetic filenames; representative real-media validation is not required unless filesystem apply policy changes.
prior_audit_relationship: New current-hash configuration interaction; no current finding described the all-options branch or global fallback.

title: Numeric-hyphen show names are rejected before supported episode tokens are parsed
observed_behavior: The noncanonical numeric-range guard scans the entire filename stem before the explicit E01/Episode/Ep and bare-episode branches run. A valid name such as 9-1-1 E01.mkv is returned as unreliable noncanonical-range, while the same show with S01E01 parses successfully.
expected_invariant: A supported episode token must be parsed in its own syntactic context; numeric-hyphen text in the show or episode title must not be treated as an episode range.
root_cause: TV_NONCANONICAL_RANGE_PATTERN is applied globally whenever the strongest token is not canonical SxxExx. The early return does not exclude text before a recognized explicit/bare episode token, even though later branches support those token forms.
failure_scenario: A source for the show 9-1-1 uses the documented E01 form and a supplied/default season. Rename preview reports a range-format error and blocks the row, so the operator cannot use the supported automatic naming workflow without manually rewriting the source name or switching token formats.
evidence: tv.py lines 531-539 runs the broad range guard before folder and episode-identity construction.
tv.py lines 565-594 explicitly supports E01/Episode/Ep and bare episode tokens after that guard.
A bundled-Python reproduction returned reliable=false and parse_mode=noncanonical-range for 9-1-1 E01.mkv, but reliable=true for 9-1-1 S01E01.mkv.
Current tests cover malformed ranges and exempt title ranges only when SxxExx is present; no numeric-hyphen show with an explicit episode-only token is covered.
Structured current-finding searches found no matching false-positive range guard.
existing_safeguards: Canonical SxxExx tokens bypass the broad noncanonical-range guard.
The parser fails closed rather than performing an ambiguous rename.
Manual naming remains available as an operator workaround.
safeguard_gap: Fail-closed behavior is correct for an actual malformed range but the guard cannot distinguish show-title text from episode syntax, so it blocks an explicitly supported unambiguous token.
tests_present: tests/python/desktop/test_service_rename_tv.py covers malformed ranges, canonical range precedence, explicit episode tokens, and numeric title ranges with SxxExx.
tests_missing: 9-1-1 E01 and other numeric-hyphen show names with Episode/Ep/bare supported forms.
Numeric ranges in episode titles for every supported episode-token form.
Negative cases proving true malformed ranges remain blocked after contextual scoping.
recommended_remediation: Parse the supported episode token first, then limit noncanonical-range detection to the episode-syntax region or explicitly exclude the show/title spans. Add positive numeric-hyphen title cases alongside the existing malformed-range negatives.
remediation_risk: low-to-medium: relaxing a fail-closed parser guard can admit ambiguous names, so keep bounded syntax rules and preserve all malformed-range regression cases
validation_rung: Focused TV parser, folder-season, rename planner/preview/apply, and bad-case corpus tests with synthetic filenames; representative real-media validation is not required.
prior_audit_relationship: New current-hash parser ordering defect; no current finding described numeric-hyphen title rejection.

title: Movie cleaner deletes meaningful parenthetical title text
observed_behavior: Both cleaner branches remove every balanced parenthetical, bracketed, or braced fragment from the selected title region. Meaningful title text is therefore indistinguishable from metadata: Birdman or (The Unexpected Virtue of Ignorance) (2014).mkv and Birdman or (2014).mkv both normalize to Birdman or (2014).
expected_invariant: Verified release metadata may be removed, but punctuation-delimited content inside the title region must be preserved unless it independently matches bounded metadata evidence.
root_cause: After selecting the title region, _normalize_movie_title_region unconditionally strips bracket contents in repeated global substitutions; the nondefault-options branch duplicates the same unconditional stripping.
failure_scenario: A movie whose canonical title contains a subtitle, qualifier, or other identity-bearing parenthetical is previewed as a different shorter movie. If the operator confirms it, the destination filename loses title identity and can collide semantically with another release even though the source bytes remain intact.
evidence: movie.py lines 468-475 globally replace every (), [], and {} fragment before term or tail classification.
movie.py lines 643-650 repeats the same behavior in the nondefault-options branch.
A bundled-Python reproduction produced the same Birdman or (2014) output with and without the identity-bearing parenthetical subtitle.
The current movie cleaner tests cover bracketed year precedence and metadata but contain no meaningful parenthetical title case.
Structured current-finding searches found no matching bracketed-title loss.
affected_flows: canonical title identity and library matching
collision review for similarly named films
existing_safeguards: Rename apply requires strict confirmation and a current preview fingerprint.
The source media contents are not transcoded by the rename workflow.
Manual movie-title override can preserve a title if the operator recognizes the loss.
safeguard_gap: Preview/confirmation show the shortened result but do not distinguish intentional metadata cleanup from an unexpected loss of canonical title text, and automatic cleaning offers no evidence-based bracket classification.
tests_present: tests/python/desktop/test_service_rename_movie.py covers year selection, verified metadata tails, and metadata-like plain title words.
tests_missing: Canonical movie titles containing meaningful parentheses, brackets, or braces.
Bracketed metadata-tail cases proving metadata still cleans without global title deletion.
Collision/identity case for two titles differentiated only by parenthetical text.
recommended_remediation: Preserve bracketed content in the chosen title region by default. Remove it only when a bounded classifier proves it is year/release metadata, and add canonical-title fixtures that retain meaningful parenthetical subtitles.
remediation_risk: medium: changing title normalization can alter many previews and destination names; compare the rename bad-case corpus and retain strict preview/apply freshness checks
validation_rung: Focused movie cleaner, rename planner/preview/apply, collision, and bad-case corpus tests using synthetic filenames; representative real-media validation is not required.
prior_audit_relationship: Related to W04-008 through title preservation, but distinct because it occurs under default options and is caused by unconditional bracket deletion rather than the nondefault global-token fallback.

title: Punctuation-equivalent shows bypass the overlapping-episode guard
observed_behavior: The planner computes normalized destination identity keys for TV rows, but its overlapping-interval loop groups shows only by raw case-folded show text. Punctuation-equivalent names such as A-B and A B normalize to the same show identity yet are treated as different, so overlapping episode rows remain ready.
expected_invariant: All collision and overlap checks for a TV plan must use the same canonical show identity as durable destination/undo evidence, so equivalent punctuation cannot evade duplicate-episode blocking.
root_cause: The overlap loop reimplements show comparison with str(show).casefold() instead of reusing the punctuation-normalized identity logic in tv_identity_key or a shared show-key helper.
failure_scenario: Two selected files parse as A-B S01E01-E02 and A B S01E02. They target distinct literal filenames, so exact destination collision does not trigger; the raw show comparison also differs. Both rows remain ready even though their canonical show identity and episode interval overlap, allowing confirmed apply to create duplicate logical episodes under punctuation variants.
evidence: planner.py lines 355-371 compares only raw case-folded show strings before checking season and interval overlap.
tv.py lines 495-497 already canonicalizes all nonalphanumeric show separators to spaces for destination_identity_key.
A bundled-Python synthetic plan produced ready rows with no errors for A-B - S01E01-E02.mkv and A B - S01E02.mkv; their normalized show identity is the same.
The current overlap test uses identical show strings and therefore cannot exercise punctuation-equivalent identity.
Structured current-finding searches found no matching logical-overlap escape.
existing_safeguards: Exact literal destination collisions are blocked.
Overlaps are blocked when parsed show strings match after case-folding.
Rows carry a normalized destination_identity_key and apply requires strict confirmation/freshness evidence.
safeguard_gap: Exact path checks cannot catch distinct punctuation spellings, and the overlap guard ignores the normalized identity already computed for each row.
tests_present: tests/python/desktop/test_service_rename_planner.py covers exact destination duplicates and overlapping episode intervals for identical show text.
tests_missing: Punctuation/whitespace-equivalent show names with overlapping single and ranged episodes.
Parity assertion that overlap grouping and destination identity use the same show normalization.
recommended_remediation: Extract one canonical TV show-key helper and use it in tv_identity_key and the planner overlap grouping. Add punctuation-equivalent overlap regressions while retaining nonoverlap and exact-path collision behavior.
remediation_risk: low-to-medium: stronger grouping can newly block plans whose punctuation differences were intentional, so expose the canonical identity in error evidence and retain an explicit manual override path if policy permits
validation_rung: Focused TV identity, rename planner/preview/apply, collision, and undo-evidence tests using synthetic files; representative real-media validation is not required.
prior_audit_relationship: New current-hash collision-policy inconsistency; no current finding described the normalized-key/raw-show split.
